source_method: S13-S18 are fictional challenge briefs with deliberately under-expressive authored draft dialogue. The drafts are not model outputs, natural baselines, review results, videos, ratings, or evidence of method superiority.
language_policy: S15 and S16 use Mandarin Chinese. S13, S14, S17, and S18 use English. Every condition within a story uses the same language.

anger.label: 愤怒
anger.meaning: Anger at another person's unilateral action.

disgust.label: 厌恶
disgust.meaning: Revulsion toward a spoiled drink's smell.

fear.label: 恐惧
fear.meaning: Shared apprehension about an uncertain physical danger.

sadness.label: 悲伤
sadness.meaning: Personal grief over an irreversible but bounded loss.

challenge_policy.purpose: Test whether each review protocol identifies and improves emotion clarity, reciprocal response, and naturalness when the shared draft is intentionally understated.
challenge_policy.frozen_inputs: All conditions must start from the exact same authored draft and share story, actions, framing, duration, references, voices, ambience, seed, and video settings. Only dialogue may change.
challenge_policy.draft_status: The draft is an authored stress-test fixture and must never be described as a spontaneous planning-model baseline.
challenge_policy.no_forced_change: A reviewer may validly retain the draft. No condition is required to edit, and no manual change may be inserted after seeing outputs.
challenge_policy.no_superiority_claim: Because the inputs were selected to invite revision, results may illustrate behavior on challenge cases but cannot independently prove MoodCut outperforms Generic Review.
challenge_policy.execution_dependency: The current scene evaluation config does not automatically inject draft-dialogue.json into a generated initial plan. Paid execution requires an explicit shared-draft adapter and offline identity tests first.

reference_selection.rule: Reuse each existing character pair once and copy its two asset records byte-for-byte; select no new images.

scope_limits: Each emotion appears in one story, so emotion, plot, cast, and film remain confounded.
The deliberately weak drafts create selection bias and are unsuitable as an unbiased benchmark without a separately preregistered protocol.
Do not replace drafts or scenarios after observing review outputs, videos, or scores.
VEMOCLAP probabilities measure whole-video emotion recognition, not dialogue quality or review correctness.

stories.title: A unilateral decision
stories.design_question: Can review make anger and opposition clear without adding the unspecified decision or aggression?

stories.title: The spoiled drink
stories.design_question: Can review strengthen revulsion while avoiding illness, drinking, or exaggerated gagging?

stories.title: A crack beneath the bridge
stories.design_question: Can review turn risk description into reciprocal fear without inventing collapse or escape?

stories.title: The approval arrives
stories.design_question: Can review make shared joy audible without adding a celebration or reward?

stories.title: The old tree is gone
stories.design_question: Can review express personal sadness and comfort without inventing backstory or a solution?

stories.title: The room is already ready
stories.design_question: Can review make disbelief clear while preserving the ordinary completed task?
